sections.overview: This seahorse occurs in the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean; records span European and North African coasts.
sections.identification: It has a short, upturned snout, a prominent spine above each eye and a body that may reach about 15 cm.
sections.habitat: It is reported in shallow muddy or rocky coastal waters, including estuaries and areas with seaweed or seagrass.
sections.diet: Seahorses take small live crustaceans; the species account notes mysid shrimps among recorded prey.
sections.behavior: It anchors itself to nearby vegetation or other surfaces with its prehensile tail and is a relatively weak swimmer.
sections.reproduction: The male carries developing eggs in a brood pouch and releases live young after they hatch.
sections.ecology: Available biological information is limited; MarLIN notes that dispersal and recovery are poorly documented.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports the global IUCN category Data Deficient, assessed in 2017; a regional assessment should not be substituted for it.
